# pgmpy
> pgmpy is a Python library for causal inference, probabilistic modeling, Bayesian networks, and directed acyclic graphs.

## Pages

### Home
- [Key Features](https://pgmpy.org/dev/index.html): pgmpy documentation for causal discovery, model testing, causal effect estimation, parameter estimation, probabilistic and causal inference, and simulations in Python.

### Getting Started
- [Getting Started](https://pgmpy.org/dev/started/index.html): Install pgmpy, try a short example for each task, and read the pgmpy license.
- [Installation](https://pgmpy.org/dev/started/install.html): pgmpy supports Python 3.10 to 3.15. For most users, the base install from PyPI is sufficient:
- [Quickstart](https://pgmpy.org/dev/started/quickstart.html): This page gives a short example for each task in pgmpy. Each section also links to the User Guide page for that task.
- [Contributing to pgmpy](https://pgmpy.org/dev/started/contributing.html): Thank you for your contribution to **pgmpy**. Use the links below for common actions. Then read the sections that follow.
- [License](https://pgmpy.org/dev/started/license.html): The MIT License (MIT)

### Guides
- [User Guide](https://pgmpy.org/dev/documentation.html): pgmpy guides for causal discovery, parameter estimation, probabilistic inference, simulations, and custom models.
- [Causal Discovery and Structure Learning](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/causal_discovery.html): Learn causal graphs from data with the causal discovery algorithms in pgmpy.
- [Causal Estimation](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/causal_estimation.html): Estimate causal effects from a graph and data with pgmpy.
- [Causal Identification](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/causal_identification.html): Find adjustment sets and frontdoor sets in causal graphs with pgmpy.
- [Defining a Custom Model](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/custom_model.html): Make custom pgmpy models and add the correct CPD or factor types.
- [Example Datasets](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/datasets.html): Find and load the benchmark datasets in pgmpy.
- [Example Models](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/example_models.html): Find and load the example models in pgmpy.
- [Extensibility](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/extensibility.html): Use the repository templates to add datasets, models, metrics, and discovery algorithms to pgmpy.
- [Exporting / Importing Models](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/io.html): Read and write pgmpy models with the save and load methods and the readwrite classes.
- [Metrics](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/metrics.html): Evaluate learned graphs and fitted models with the metrics in pgmpy.
- [Parameter Estimation](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/parameter_estimation.html): Estimate the parameters of a model from data with pgmpy.
- [Plotting Models](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/plotting.html): Draw pgmpy graphs with Graphviz, daft, or networkx.
- [Probabilistic Inference](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/probabilistic_inference.html): Query fitted pgmpy models with the probabilistic inference algorithms.
- [Simulations](https://pgmpy.org/dev/guides/simulations.html): Generate synthetic data from fitted pgmpy models.

### Examples
- [Example Notebooks](https://pgmpy.org/dev/examples.html): pgmpy example notebooks about Bayesian networks, structure learning, inference, simulations, and causal analysis.

### API Reference
- [API Reference](https://pgmpy.org/dev/reference.html): Public API reference for pgmpy graphs, models, factors, inference, discovery, metrics, datasets, example models, and model import or export.
- [Graph Classes](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/base.html): The graph classes that pgmpy models, discovery algorithms, and causal methods use.
- [Causal Inference](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/causal_inference.html): Public classes for identification, interventional queries, and regression-based causal effect estimation.
- [Conditional Independence (CI) Tests](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/ci_test.html): The function that selects a CI test, and the CI tests.
- [Datasets and Example Models](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/data.html): The functions that find and load datasets and example models.
- [Factors and CPDs](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/factors.html): The factor, CPD, and factor-container classes that define the parameters of pgmpy models.
- [Independencies](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/independencies.html): Classes for independence assertions and collections of independencies.
- [Inference and Sampling](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/inference.html): 
- [Metrics](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/metrics.html): Metrics that evaluate learned structures, implied independencies, and fitted models.
- [Models](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/models.html): Public model classes for probabilistic, causal, and structural-equation workflows.
- [Parameter Estimation](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/parameter_estimation.html): Estimator classes that fit model parameters and related marginal representations to data.
- [Reading/Writing](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/readwrite.html): Reader and writer classes for the file formats that pgmpy supports.
- [Causal Discovery and Structure Learning](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/structure_learning.html): Discovery algorithms and expert-guided methods that learn the graph structure from data.
- [Structure Scoring](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/structure_score.html): Structure score classes for score-based discovery.
- [Tags](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/tags.html): pgmpy objects describe themselves with `skbase <https://skbase.readthedocs.io>`_ tags. For example, tags give the data types that a causal discovery algorithm accepts, or the assumptions of its guarantees. Read tags with ``get_tag`` or ``get_class_tag``. Use :func:`skbase.lookup.all_objects` to find objects by their tags:
- [Undirected Model Index](https://pgmpy.org/dev/api/undirected.html): This page lists only the undirected models. The full list is in the :doc:`Models </api/models>` reference.

### Project
- [Getting Involved](https://pgmpy.org/dev/development.html): How to contribute to pgmpy, report issues, open pull requests, and contact the community.
- [Citation](https://pgmpy.org/dev/citation.html): If you use pgmpy in your scientific work, cite this paper:
- [References](https://pgmpy.org/dev/references.html): This page lists the research papers and resources that pgmpy uses for its implementations.
- [Supported By](https://pgmpy.org/dev/supported_by.html): The grants, programs, and sponsors that give financial support to pgmpy.
- [Tutorial Notebooks](https://pgmpy.org/dev/tutorial.html): pgmpy tutorial notebooks about probabilistic graphical models, Bayesian networks, inference, learning, and case studies.
